content.text:
<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9358, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

export function previewSrc(att: Attachment): string | null {
  if (att.dataUrl) return att.dataUrl;
  const p = att.preview;
  if (!p) return null;
  if (PALETTES[p]) return landscape(p);
  if (p.startsWith('ui')) return uiMock(Number(p.slice(2)) || 1, '#0b57d0');
  if (p === 'chart') return chart('#0b57d0');
  if (p === 'blueprint') return blueprint();
  if (p === 'confetti') return confetti();
  if (p.startsWith('portrait')) return portrait(Number(p.slice(8)) || 200);
  return null;
}

function pdfEscape(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/[\\()]/g, (c) => `\\${c}`).replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g, '-');
}

export function buildPdf(title: string, lines: string[]): Blob {
  const content = [
    'BT /F1 22 Tf 60 760 Td (' + pdfEscape(title) + ') Tj ET',
    ...lines.map((l, i) => `BT /F1 12 Tf 60 ${720 - i * 20} Td (${pdfEscape(l)}) Tj ET`),
  ].join('\n');
  const objects = [
    '<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>',
    '<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>',
    '<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents 4 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R >> >> >>',
    `<< /Length ${content.length} >>\nstream\n${content}\nendstream`,
    '<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>',
  ];
  let out = '%PDF-1.4\n';
  const offsets: number[] = [];
  objects.forEach((o, i) => {
    offsets.push(out.length);
    out += `${i + 1} 0 obj\n${o}\nendobj\n`;
  });
  const xref = out.length;
  out += `xref\n0 ${objects.length + 1}\n0000000000 65535 f \n`;
  offsets.forEach((off) => {
    out += `${String(off).padStart(10, '0')} 00000 n \n`;
  });
  out += `trailer\n<< /Size ${objects.length + 1} /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n${xref}\n%%EOF`;
  return new Blob([out], { type: 'application/pdf' });
}

export async function downloadAttachment(att: Attachment) {
  const { downloadBlob } = await import('./utils');
  if (att.dataUrl) {
    const res = await fetch(att.dataUrl);
    downloadBlob(await res.blob(), att.name);
    return;
  }
  const kind = fileKind(att.name, att.type).kind;
  const src = previewSrc(att);
  if (kind === 'image' && src) {
    const img = new Image();
    img.src = src;
    await img.decode();
    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    canvas.width = img.naturalWidth || 640;
    canvas.height = img.naturalHeight || 420;
    canvas.getContext('2d')!.drawImage(img, 0, 0);
    canvas.toBlob((b) => b && downloadBlob(b, att.name.replace(/\.\w+$/, '.png')), 'image/png');
    return;
  }
  if (kind === 'pdf') {
    downloadBlob(
      buildPdf(att.name.replace(/\.pdf$/i, ''), [
        'This document was generated by the local demo mailbox.',
        `Original attachment: ${att.name}`,
        `Reported size: ${Math.round(att.size / 1024)} KB`,
        '',
        'No external services were contacted to produce this file.',
      ]),
      att.name,
    );
    return;
  }
  downloadBlob(
    new Blob([`${att.name}\n\nDemo attachment from the local mailbox.\nReported size: ${att.size} bytes\n`], { type: 'text/plain' }),
    `${att.name}.txt`,
  );
}

# Claude Opus 5.5

A Gmail-style mail client that runs entirely in the browser. No accounts, servers or API keys: the mailbox is seeded locally and persisted in `localStorage`, so it works offline and survives reloads.

## Run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:9358
```

Other scripts:

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | Typecheck, then production build to `dist/` |
| `pnpm preview` | Serve the production build on port 9358 |
| `pnpm typecheck` | TypeScript only |

The Gmail-style app is built and running at http://localhost:9358. Typecheck and production build pass, and all 24 browser workflow tests pass on desktop and mobile with no console or page errors. The browser tab title and the header title both read exactly "Claude Opus 5.5".

What the tests cover, run with `pnpm e2e` against local Chrome:
- **Mailbox basics:** category tabs, starring, opening a conversation, and checking that the message thread displays properly.
- **Replies and archiving:** replying inline, then archiving from the thread toolbar and undoing it.
- **List actions:** selecting multiple conversations to mark read or unread, applying a label, deleting to Trash, and snoozing.
- **Search:** suggestions, plus operator searches like `has:attachment from:priya`.
- **Compose:** contact autocomplete, bold formatting, sending into Sent, the forgotten-attachment warning, and closing a message to save it as a draft.
- **Shortcuts and views:** keyboard shortcuts (`j`/`k`/`o`/`u`/`e`/`?`), attachment preview, split reading pane with dark theme, the settings page, and data surviving a reload.
- **Mobile:** slide-out menu, the conversation view, full-screen reply, and the Compose button.

A separate script (`scripts/reply-check.mjs`) confirmed that after you send to a contact, a simulated reply lands about 20 seconds later with a "New message from Priya" toast.

Testing turned up three real bugs, now fixed:
- **Truncated title:** the desktop header was cutting the title to "Claude Opus…".
- **Compose window position:** it sat partly off-screen at the left because two conflicting CSS classes were fighting, and the wrong one won.
- **Narrow split view:** the category tabs were squeezed into unreadable stubs. They now switch to icons with count badges when the list is narrow.

A few things you should know:
- **Unsubscribe works:** clicking Unsubscribe on a sender actually stops that sender's queued incoming mail.
- **Undo returns you to the thread:** if you archive from an open conversation and hit Undo, you land back in that conversation, like Gmail.
- **The app warns before some sends:** a message with no subject, or one that mentions an attachment with none attached, gets a confirm dialog first.

Everything is saved in the browser's local storage, and "Reset demo mailbox" in the avatar menu or in Settings → Advanced restores the original sample mail. - **Compose window check:** this was the debug run that found the compose window stuck at the left edge, which is fixed.
- **Three test runs:** these were earlier rounds of the browser tests. The last one passed all 24 checks, and the later production build succeeded.

The app is still running at http://localhost:9358.
